```plato
    // The (column, row, layer) triple for a row-major flat index. Inverse of FlattenIndex.
    UnflattenIndex(self: IIndexable3D<$T>, index: Integer): Tuple3<Integer, Integer, Integer>
        => (index % self.ColumnCount,
            (index / self.ColumnCount) % self.RowCount,
            index / (self.ColumnCount * self.RowCount));

    // The first cell (0, 0, 0). Precondition: not empty.
    FirstCell(self: IIndexable3D<$T>): $T
        => self.At(0, 0, 0);

    // The last cell. Precondition: not empty.
    LastCell(self: IIndexable3D<$T>): $T
        => self.At(self.ColumnCount - 1, self.RowCount - 1, self.LayerCount - 1);

    //==
    // # Collections indexable
    //
    // Derived functionality for ICountable, IIndex and one-dimensional IIndexable
    // (`collections.concepts.plato`): emptiness tests, typed-index
    // predicates, endpoint access, and the fold / map family
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(higher-order_function)).
    //
    // This file also carries the shared provenance note for the whole
    // `collections-*` / `functional-*` library family, which was split out of a
    // single combined collections-and-functional library.
    //
    // Bodies for the interfaces declared in `collections.concepts.plato`,
    // `collections.concepts.plato` and
    // `functional.concepts.plato`. Every function's first parameter is
    // interface-typed, so it becomes available on every implementing type. Pure
    // expressions only; collections are immutable, so "modifying" helpers return
    // new values. See `../README.md` for conventions.

    //==
    // # ICountable
    //
    // Emptiness tests derived from the element count.

    // True when the collection has no elements.
    IsEmpty(self: ICountable): Boolean
        => self.Count == 0;

    // True when the collection has at least one element.
    IsNotEmpty(self: ICountable): Boolean
        => self.Count > 0;

    // True when the collection holds exactly one element.
    IsSingleton(self: ICountable): Boolean
        => self.Count == 1;

    //==
    // # IIndex
    //
    // A typed zero-based position; Value == -1 is the "none" sentinel.

    // True when the index refers to nothing. A negative value means none,
    // conventionally -1.
    IsNone(self: IIndex): Boolean
        => self.Value < 0;

    // True when the index refers to a real position (non-negative).
    IsPresent(self: IIndex): Boolean
        => self.Value >= 0;

    // The digest of a typed index. Every IIndex implementor is a single-field
    // wrapper over Integer, so the raw value's hash is the whole content of the
    // value and is therefore consistent with structural equality by construction.
    Hash(self: IIndex): Integer
        => self.Value.Hash;

    // The natural total order on typed indices: compare the raw positions. This
    // is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive because Integer's order is, and
    // it agrees with equality because Value is the only field. The "none"
    // sentinel (-1) sorts below every present position, which is the conventional
    // reading. Discharges the IOrderable obligation for every IIndex implementor;
    // IComparable.Compare then follows from Core's Compare(IOrderable).
    LessThanOrEquals(a: IIndex, b: IIndex): Boolean
        => a.Value <= b.Value;

    // Deliberately NOT covered here: MortonCode2D/3D (spatial-structures) and
    // FontWeight (text) are also single-`Value: Integer` wrappers, but they do
    // not implement IIndex and must not — they are opaque codes, not element
    // references (README, "typed index types" convention). No interface-typed
    // generic can reach them; their Hash / LessThanOrEquals are concrete
    // obligations for P8 and the text domain respectively.
    // TODO(cross-package): concrete Hash/LessThanOrEquals for those three.

    //==
    // # IIndexable
    //
    // Endpoint access and bounds checking for a one-dimensional collection.

    // The index of the last element (Count - 1); negative when empty.
    LastIndex(self: IIndexable<$T>): Integer
        => self.Count - 1;

    // True when index lies within [0, Count).
    IsValidIndex(self: IIndexable<$T>, index: Integer): Boolean
        => index >= 0 && index < self.Count;

    // Element access via a typed IIndex wrapper. Precondition: the index is present.
    At(self: IIndexable<$T>, index: IIndex): $T
        => self[index.Value];

    // True when a typed IIndex refers to a real position within [0, Count).
    IsValidIndex(self: IIndexable<$T>, index: IIndex): Boolean
        => index.Value >= 0 && index.Value < self.Count;

    // The first element. Precondition: the collection is not empty.
    First(self: IIndexable<$T>): $T
        => self[0];

    // The last element. Precondition: the collection is not empty.
    Last(self: IIndexable<$T>): $T
        => self[self.Count - 1];

    // The middle element (rounding the index down). Precondition: not empty.
    Middle(self: IIndexable<$T>): $T
        => self[self.Count / 2];

    //==
    // # IIndexable — fold / map family
    //
    // The general element-traversal primitives, usable on ANY IIndexable rather
    // than only on the concrete Array intrinsics. Each first materializes the
    // elements in index order via `MapRange(Count, i => At(i))` and then defers
    // to the corresponding Array intrinsic. Written with >= 2 parameters carrying
    // a type variable, so they clear the FunctionInstance single-type-var guard.

    // Folds the elements left to right from an initial accumulator: applies
    // f(acc, element) across the collection in index order. The general reduction
    // primitive behind sums, extents, and running aggregates on any indexable.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(higher-order_function))
    Reduce(xs: IIndexable<$T>, acc: $U, f: Function2<$U, $T, $U>): $U
        => MapRange(xs.Count, i => xs[i]).Reduce(acc, f);

    // A new Array holding f applied to each element in index order.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Map_(higher-order_function))
    Map(xs: IIndexable<$T>, f: Function1<$T, $U>): Array<$U>
        => MapRange(xs.Count, i => xs[i]).Map(f);

    // True when every element satisfies the predicate (vacuously true when empty).
    All(xs: IIndexable<$T>, predicate: Function1<$T, Boolean>): Boolean
        => MapRange(xs.Count, i => xs[i]).All(predicate);

    // True when at least one element satisfies the predicate (false when empty).
    Any(xs: IIndexable<$T>, predicate: Function1<$T, Boolean>): Boolean
        => MapRange(xs.Count, i => xs[i]).Any(predicate);
```
